personas.backstory: Has held a seat on the Hrastovec council since the second winter of the Oath. Keeps a ledger of who owes favours in Ukrenvar and who has forgotten them. Lost the Vodnagrad vote to {rival} by three hands and has been quietly counting those hands ever since.
catchphrases: A matter for the council, {player}. Come find me.
Curious that {rival} keeps missing the vote, {player}.

personas.backstory: Runs a wool and salt route between Brezhnik and Mokrenka and has never lost a cart to a bandit without bargaining with him afterwards. Took a 40 gold toll from {rival} after an ambush on the Lipnevo road and still sends them a discount letter every week.
catchphrases: Grudges cost coin, {player}. Let's talk prices.
Horses are half price if you ask nicely.

personas.backstory: Swore a feast-oath in Hrastovec hall that Tesnovar's banners would fly over Ostrogrado before the new moon. The moon has turned three times since. Yielded the field to {rival} at Smrekovo and calls the defeat a lesson sent by the ancestors.
catchphrases: Hark! Tesnovar's oath still binds us all.
Well struck, ser {player}. The ancestors approve.

personas.backstory: Has held the fords of Redlice since the first war and still remembers the winter the fens flooded Gorvenka. Tells newcomers to stock food before crossing. Once taught {rival} to hold a charge line at Stribogra, and bore no grudge when they used it on him.
catchphrases: Pack bread for two days before the fens, friend.
Good form, {player}. That feint was clean.

personas.backstory: Trades dyed wool and dried fish along the Dubnyak and Zhelnice roads. Refuses to pay bandit tolls and says so loudly. Took a thistle-bordered bolt of cloth from {rival} as payment and has been trying to resell it ever since.
catchphrases: dyed wool moving fast, {player}. make an offer.
salt prices again. somebody sell me a cheaper road.

personas.backstory: Has burned more fields around Vezhdrak than anyone will admit, and calls the scorch marks art. Keeps a list of every insult {rival} typed since Smrekovo and reads it aloud whenever they lose a road. Still refuses to accept a rematch from anyone who beat them twice.
catchphrases: Ur banner burns better than ur army, {player}!!!
Still counting. {rival} owes me 3 insults and a rematch.

personas.backstory: Joined when the Ukrenvar road was still a mud track and has been picking fights on it ever since. Known for quick insults and quicker retreats. Beat {rival} twice at Brusnice and has never admitted the second win was close, only that it was a mistake.
catchphrases: lmao ur flag looks sad from up here
{player} took the bait again. shocking

personas.backstory: Tracks troop ratios in every siege since the Vrasnik campaign and posts the numbers after each defeat. Took Lyutoda in under two days with a 3:1 cavalry edge. Considers {rival} a tactical disappointment, mostly for poor archer positioning.
catchphrases: gg. the ratio was off, not the plan
gg {player}. ur line broke at 40 percent

personas.backstory: Declared war on the bridge at Mokrenka after it refused to let a sacred goose cross, and has filed complaints about it ever since. Gives everyone nicknames, including the Smrekovo reeve. Lost a duel to {rival} and blames the sun, which is the sun's fault.
catchphrases: The goose of Redlice is avenged!! Respect the goose
{player} i forgive u. the goose does not

personas.backstory: Keeps a small oat-field near Sedlov and has sworn never to march farther than the Chorvena ford. Has stood with the Wardenry since the first war. Yielded a sword duel to {rival} at Bukhrov and calls it a debt the ancestors will collect.
catchphrases: By the oath of Lisnik Gate, I hold this road.
Ser {player}, the ancestors will remember that blow.
